rules.rule: Adjectivally used participles agree in gender, number and case, with the strong/weak choices already taught for adjectives. Present -ende follows the grēne-type strong declension; it is not a masculine agent noun in -end.

Cook61: present participles in the predicate as nominative/accusative are generally uninflected. Cook62: predicate past participles are generally indeclinable or take strong masculine endings. Cook179 allows uninflected predicate participles. Thus neuterplural dēor bunden is acceptable; dēor bundene is also licensed in verbal passive usage. Do not judge them by an obligatory attributive neuter-u rule.

Heavy-stem disyllabic participles can lose the unstressed vowel before vowel-initial inflections: bundenes→bundnes, bundenum→bundnum; hīeredes→hīerdes, hīeredum→hīerdum, hīerede→hīerde. Full vowels are often restored in West Saxon. Keep the full stem before -ne/-re/-ra; doubled n in bundenne is ordinary. Short-root fręmed/nęred and lufod retain their vowel in the selected model. Rare -u cells above are transparently paradigm-derived.

Weak participles are lexical principal parts, not a universal past-minus-e shortcut: hīerde→hīered, fręmede→fręmed, lufode→lufod, sealde→seald, worhte→worht, sętte→sętt, sęnde→sęnd, lǣdde→lǣd. Before inflection, syncope can bring a dental into contact with a voiceless stem and cause -t-, as Fulk113 scierped→scierpte. These audit examples do not newly assign unlisted verbs.

A past participle of an intransitive verb need not be passive. Source wæs geworden is a become/come-to-pass resultative closure, not a transitive passive. Auxiliary tense does not force one Modern English tense/aspect translation.
